title: Tenant-aware circuit breaker + safe fallback strategy for model & dependency failures
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: Implement multi-tier circuit breakers that operate at three scopes — dependency (external services like embedder/redis), model (model runtime & variant), and tenant (customer-level noisy-neighbor protection). The circuit breakers must: 1) detect degraded health via error rate, latency, and resource-exhaustion signals; 2) trip in a predictable way with conservative false-positive avoidance; 3) support safe fallback behaviors (cache, cheaper model variant, limited feature set); 4) expose metrics and traces for SRE/PM to tune thresholds; 5) allow per-tenant overrides and global defaults; 6) integrate with multi-region failover and load-shedding policies.
design_decisions_and_tradeoffs:
- Scope: We implement three independent but cooperating CB layers. Dependency CBs are owned by infra teams and are aggressive for external third-party calls. Model CBs live in the serving runtime and are model/variant aware. Tenant CBs run in the routing layer to preserve a tenant's apps from noisy neighbors.
- Thresholds: Use hybrid thresholds (error-rate + p95 latency + resource flags) over a sliding window (5m default) with minimum request volume check to avoid spurious trips. This avoids tripping on rare spikes.
- Reaction: When tripped, apply graduated fallbacks rather than hard failures: try cached responses -> fallback model variant (quantized/shorter context) -> degrade features (disable function-calls or streaming) -> request shed. Hard failure only when none available.
- Testing: Emulate failures in staging with chaos experiments and synthetic tenants to validate stability and avoid cascading trips across regions.
- Tradeoffs: Conservatively set default thresholds to minimize user-visible regressions; expose tenant overrides for power users but require guardrails to prevent abuse. More aggressive defaults reduce tail SLO breaches but increase risk of incorrect fallbacks.
- Backoff and half-open: Exponential backoff with jitter and a limited half-open probe window (e.g., allow 5 test requests every 30s) to reduce flapping.
- Observability: Emit 'circuit_breaker.state' metric with tags {scope, id, reason, tenant, model, region}. Capture event logs for every trip/reset with sample payloads to aid debugging.
trip_thresholds_and_algorithms:
Default hybrid trip policy (configurable per scope):
- Window: sliding 5m, step 10s, min_volume = 100 requests.
- Error-rate rule: trip when 5xx_rate >= 5% AND requests >= min_volume.
- Latency rule: trip when p95_latency >= 800ms AND requests >= min_volume.
- Resource rule: trip immediately on detected resource-exhaustion signals (OOM, GPU memory pressure, kernel retries) reported by agent.
- Combined rule: trip if any two of the three rules (error, latency, resource) are true OR resource rule alone.
- Tenant-specific caps: additionally trip when tenant_quota_utilization >= 95% and tenant_tokens_per_minute increases > 3x baseline for 2 consecutive windows.
- Model-level policy: prefer variant-aware fallback; e.g., if gpt-xl-int8 has errors, fallback to gpt-large-quantized; if both fail, fallback to short-context variant that disables convo-history expansion.
- Dependency CB: more aggressive (trip at 2% 5xx over 1m) for external vendors to avoid cascading timeouts in our runtime.
fallback_behaviors:
Ordered fallback pipeline (attempt each step before escalating):
1) Short TTL prefix cache: return cached response if confidence score >= 0.75 and cache_age <= 30s.
2) Model variant fallback: route to same-architecture quantized/shorter-context variant. Response decorated with header 'x-redwood-fallback: model-variant'.
3) Response degradation: remove non-critical fields (e.g., omit long tool traces or extra metadata), disable streaming to reduce runtime pressure.
4) Graceful placeholder: return deterministic minimal reply (e.g., 'We are experiencing high load; please retry in a few seconds') for explicit conversational flows.
5) Rate-limited shedding: reject with 429 + structured JSON pointing to retry-after and support links.
Notes: Each fallback emits explicit telemetry with fallback_reason and fallback_step. Fallbacks for P0 customers default to more conservative steps (prefer model fallback over throwing 429).
configuration_example:
# Sample circuit-breaker config (YAML semantics shown as string)
cb_defaults:
  window: 300  # seconds (5m)
  min_volume: 100
  error_rate_threshold: 0.05
  p95_latency_threshold_ms: 800
  probe_rate: 5   # half-open probes per window
scopes:
  dependency:
    error_rate_threshold: 0.02
    window: 60
  model:
    per_model_overrides:
      - model: 'gpt-xl'
        error_rate_threshold: 0.03
        fallback_variant: 'gpt-xl-int8'
  tenant:
    default_quota_utilization_trip: 0.95
    burst_detection_multiplier: 3
observability_and_alerting:
- Metrics: cb_tripped_total, cb_state{scope, id, reason, tenant, model, region}, cb_reset_total, cb_probe_success_total.
- Dashboards: per-region and per-tenant heatmaps showing active breakers, p95 latency, and fallback counts.
- Alerts: Page SRE on >5 unique circuits tripped in 1m in a region OR any P0 tenant receiving 10+ fallback events in 5m.
- Runbook: Add links in alert to the circuit event stream, recent traces, and tenant config UI.
- Audit logs: persist breaker decisions for 30 days for postmortem; longer retention for enterprise customers upon request.
testing_and_rollout_plan:
1) Unit tests for threshold logic and backoff math.
2) Local integration test harness that simulates error/latency traces.
3) Staging chaos experiment: inject 5xx and latency into model pods to verify fallback sequence and that tenant CB prevents noisy tenant from affecting others.
4) Canary: enable CBs in canary region for 10% traffic with detailed telemetry.
5) Gradual rollout: increase to 50% after 48h observation, then 100% after 7 days and postmortem.
6) Validation: run customer-facing QA scenarios for top 10 tenants and P0 tenants; confirm SLOs and acceptable degradation modes.
7) Post-deploy: capture metrics for 14 days to confirm false-positive rate <1% and successful recovery rate > 95%.
acceptance_criteria: Circuit breakers can be configured per-scope (dependency/model/tenant) via config service
Trip rules match the hybrid policy and are covered by unit+integration tests
Fallback pipeline executes in correct order and emits telemetry for each step
CB state and events appear in dashboards and runbook links are attached to alerts
Canary rollout shows no >10% increase in global error rate across 48h
Manual override to force-close or force-open a circuit via Console is implemented
